rationale: C22 plausibly supplied a material drafting kernel for the later letter. Both closely timed letters defend the Federal civil service and describe civil servants as loyal, career-oriented public workers whose status and treatment deserve protection. The especially close pairing of C22's “loyal hard-working civil servants,” “career civil service,” and “best interests of the Federal civil service” with the child's “loyal and reliable force,” career devotion, and concern about attacks on that force is more concrete than a merely shared topic. C13 has related career-civil-servant praise but is principally a personalized resignation letter; C09 shares an anniversary-recognition structure and praise of public servants but concerns a substantially different program.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I have found in them a loyal and reliable force, always ready to do the public's work with impartiality and diligence.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: with the possibility of injury to the loyal hard-working civil servants affected by it
shared_material.explanation: Both use closely parallel language characterizing civil servants as loyal and diligent workers while expressing concern about harm directed toward them.

shared_material.child_excerpt: creating a skilled corps of men and women with a public point of view who are willing to devote their careers to the people's business
shared_material.parent_excerpt: would afford an orderly method for absorption of such appointees into the career civil service
shared_material.explanation: Both emphasize building and preserving a career-based civil-service corps.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The people of the United States have a very great asset in this force.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am calling it to your attention as being in the best interests of the Federal civil service.
shared_material.explanation: Each closes its substantive discussion by presenting protection of the civil service as an important public or institutional interest.
